userStories.title: gitWithTimeout kills git's whole process group
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make gitWithTimeout stop git and its helpers on abort and timeout without changing its return contract.

**Motivation** — a cancelled or timed-out push or fetch can keep doing network work after nax reported it cancelled.

**Approach** — **#2900, group kill.** `gitWithTimeout` spawns git with `detached: true`, which makes the git pid the leader of a new process group, so a group kill reaches every helper git spawned. The kill does two things in order: `_gitDeps.killProcessGroup(proc.pid, "SIGKILL", { singleProcessFallback: false })`, then `proc.kill("SIGKILL")` (each in its own try). The direct `proc.kill` still reaches git where groups do not exist (Windows, where `process.kill(-pid)` throws a non-`ESRCH` error that `killProcessGroup` reports as sent). It also keeps the existing `proc.killed` assertions true. `killProcessGroup` is the existing helper in `packages/nax-agent/src/internal/process-kill.ts`. It is reached through `_gitDeps`, so fake-spawn unit tests can observe it without sending real signals; the POSIX integration test deliberately signals only the real child process group it captures. Precedent: `argvExec` in `packages/nax-agent/src/internal/argv-exec.ts` spawns `detached: true` and kills through `_argvExecDeps.killProcessGroup`. The early returns on the timeout and abort paths (no awaiting of drain promises) stay as they are. A detached git has no controlling terminal (`setsid`). nax's push paths already set `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` (`NO_TERMINAL_PROMPT` in `packages/nax/src/utils/git.ts`, used by `finish/commit.ts` and `bot/git.ts`), and a credential helper or askpass program needs no terminal. What is lost is a prompt ssh would read from `/dev/tty` itself (a key passphrase, a host-key confirmation): that call now fails at once instead of waiting on the terminal.

Fact for the test stories: `makeSpawnResult` in `packages/test-kit/src/bun/spawn.ts` reports `pid: 4242` unless told otherwise. A test that fakes `_gitDeps.spawn`, reaches a kill, and leaves `_gitDeps.killProcessGroup` at its default would send a real `SIGKILL` to process group 4242 on the machine running the tests. Five existing tests reach a kill through a faked spawn. Two are in `nax-agent`: `test/unit/internal/git-env.test.ts` (the `gitWithTimeout abort signal (#2895)` describe) and `test/unit/tools/git-commit.test.ts` (the hung `check-ignore`). Three are in `nax`: `test/unit/utils/git.test.ts` (`does not stall when git subprocess hangs`), `test/unit/bot/git.test.ts` (`AC-3 forwards the deadline and kills a hung git`) and `test/unit/review/runner.test.ts` (the `getUncommittedFilesImpl — BUG-1 pipe-drain regression` suite, which shrinks `_gitDeps.gitTimeoutMs` to 50). `_gitDeps` is one object, re-exported by `packages/nax/src/utils/git.ts`, so a patch through either path reaches it.

**Scope** — In: packages/nax-agent git execution and its local fake-spawn safety updates; create test/integration/internal/git-exec-group-kill.test.ts using the real runtime spawn on POSIX. Modify test/unit/internal/git-env.test.ts and test/unit/tools/git-commit.test.ts to install/restorably record the new seam before any fake reaches a kill, preserving existing proc.killed and result assertions. Out: US-002 owns nax caller regressions and nax fake-spawn suites; no shared test-kit pid/preload change, application-exit cleanup, or terminal-preserving SSH redesign.

**Interface** — `_gitDeps` also holds `killProcessGroup` (default: the `killProcessGroup` exported by `process-kill.ts`). The spawn options carry `detached: true`. The abort and timeout kill calls `_gitDeps.killProcessGroup(proc.pid, "SIGKILL", { singleProcessFallback: false })`, then `proc.kill("SIGKILL")`. The signature and return shape of `gitWithTimeout` are unchanged.

```typescript
killProcessGroup(pid, signal, opts?)
```

Failure handling: group-kill exceptions or unsupported process groups must not prevent direct proc.kill; each kill tolerates an exited process. Detached ssh requests requiring /dev/tty fail immediately rather than prompting. Preserve the concurrent drains and early timeout/abort returns; do not wait for a helper-held pipe to close.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] With _gitDeps.spawn faked to a hanging process and _gitDeps.killProcessGroup stubbed, gitWithTimeout(["push"], dir, 5_000, undefined, undefined, undefined, signal) spawns with options that include detached: true.
[unit] In the hanging push setup, aborting signal calls _gitDeps.killProcessGroup once with the fake's pid, "SIGKILL" and { singleProcessFallback: false }.
[unit] In the hanging push setup, aborting signal also calls the fake process's kill("SIGKILL"), after the killProcessGroup call.

[unit] With a hanging fake spawn and a stubbed _gitDeps.killProcessGroup, a gitWithTimeout(["fetch"], dir, 20) timeout calls killProcessGroup once with the fake's pid, "SIGKILL" and { singleProcessFallback: false }, and resolves { stdout: "", stderr: "", exitCode: 1, timedOut: true }.
[unit] When the stubbed _gitDeps.killProcessGroup throws, an abort still calls the fake process's kill("SIGKILL") and resolves with aborted: true.
[unit] A git call that exits 0 before any abort or timeout calls _gitDeps.killProcessGroup zero times.
[unit] _gitDeps.killProcessGroup is, by default, the killProcessGroup function exported by packages/nax-agent/src/internal/process-kill.ts.

[integration] On POSIX, with the real spawn, gitWithTimeout runs a git alias that starts a shell which starts sleep 3003 (e.g. -c alias.hang='!sh -c "sleep 3003"', giving the effective command argv ["git", "-c", ..., "hang"]; pass only the arguments after git as args, or pass full argv via argvOverride). Aborting its seventh-argument signal 200 ms after start leaves no process in the spawned git's process group alive within 2 s of the result. The test captures git's pid by wrapping _gitDeps.spawn around the real spawn, and reads group membership with ps -o pid=,pgid=.
When process groups are unavailable and killProcessGroup reports sent without killing git, aborting gitWithTimeout still calls proc.kill("SIGKILL").

When the abort signal has fired and both `killProcessGroup` and `proc.kill` throw because git already exited, `gitWithTimeout` resolves `{ stdout: "", stderr: "", exitCode: 1, aborted: true }` rather than rejecting.
When git exits normally before any abort or timeout, gitWithTimeout resolves the process's stdout, stderr and exitCode unchanged, without adding timedOut or aborted fields.

routing.reasoning: Existing process-group primitive and dependency-seam pattern; bounded execution change with local fake-signal safety and a POSIX integration regression.

modifiedFiles.reason: the `gitWithTimeout abort signal (#2895)` tests fake `_gitDeps.spawn` (pid 4242) and reach the kill; each must also replace `_gitDeps.killProcessGroup` with a recording stub (restored after the test), so no real `SIGKILL` reaches process group 4242. Their existing `proc.killed` and result assertions stay.

the test whose faked `check-ignore` hangs reaches the timeout kill through a faked spawn (pid 4242); it must also replace `_gitDeps.killProcessGroup` with a recording stub (restored after the test). Its existing assertions stay.

userStories.title: nax's git callers reach the group kill
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Verify nax's existing git entry points reach the shared group kill and make their fake-spawn regressions safe.

**Motivation** — A long `nax chat` session also gathers orphans.

**Approach** — `gitWithTimeout` spawns git with `detached: true`, which makes the git pid the leader of a new process group, so a group kill reaches every helper git spawned. The kill does two things in order: `_gitDeps.killProcessGroup(proc.pid, "SIGKILL", { singleProcessFallback: false })`, then `proc.kill("SIGKILL")` (each in its own try). The direct `proc.kill` still reaches git where groups do not exist (Windows, where `process.kill(-pid)` throws a non-`ESRCH` error that `killProcessGroup` reports as sent). It also keeps the existing `proc.killed` assertions true.

Fact for the test stories: `makeSpawnResult` in `packages/test-kit/src/bun/spawn.ts` reports `pid: 4242` unless told otherwise. A test that fakes `_gitDeps.spawn`, reaches a kill, and leaves `_gitDeps.killProcessGroup` at its default would send a real `SIGKILL` to process group 4242 on the machine running the tests. Five existing tests reach a kill through a faked spawn. Two are in `nax-agent`: `test/unit/internal/git-env.test.ts` (the `gitWithTimeout abort signal (#2895)` describe) and `test/unit/tools/git-commit.test.ts` (the hung `check-ignore`). Three are in `nax`: `test/unit/utils/git.test.ts` (`does not stall when git subprocess hangs`), `test/unit/bot/git.test.ts` (`AC-3 forwards the deadline and kills a hung git`) and `test/unit/review/runner.test.ts` (the `getUncommittedFilesImpl — BUG-1 pipe-drain regression` suite, which shrinks `_gitDeps.gitTimeoutMs` to 50). `_gitDeps` is one object, re-exported by `packages/nax/src/utils/git.ts`, so a patch through either path reaches it.

**Scope** — In: packages/nax's botGit and captureWorkingTreeChanges paths and their existing tests. test/unit/bot/git.test.ts's AC-3 hung-git test must replace/restore killProcessGroup with a recording stub and keep killed/timedOut assertions. test/unit/utils/git.test.ts's hung subprocess test must stub the same seam, observe all three calls and preserve killCount of 3 because proc.kill still runs once per call. Each test in test/unit/review/runner.test.ts's BUG-1 pipe-drain regression suite must have the stub installed and restored in afterEach, retaining existing assertions. This binding story intentionally owns caller regression/safety changes even though US-001 supplies the production behavior; do not add artificial production abstractions merely to avoid its test-focused scope. Out: changing gitWithTimeout itself and nax-agent tests belong to US-001; do not alter credentials, the shared fake pid/preload, or application-exit cleanup.

**Interface** — US-001 → US-002: `_gitDeps.killProcessGroup`, added by US-001, is called through nax's `botGit` and `captureWorkingTreeChanges`. `gitWithTimeout`'s signature and return shape remain unchanged; keep the same re-exported object, deadline forwarding, hooks-off argv and environment overlays.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] botGit(["fetch"], "/repo", 50) with _gitDeps.spawn faked to a hanging process and _gitDeps.killProcessGroup replaced by a recording stub calls the stub once with the fake's pid and "SIGKILL".
[unit] captureWorkingTreeChanges with every git call faked to hang and _gitDeps.killProcessGroup replaced by a recording stub calls the stub once per hung git call, with each fake's pid.

[unit] With a hanging fake spawn, a recording group-kill stub and proc.kill resolving the fake's exited promise, botGit(["fetch"], "/repo", 50) still resolves a result with timedOut: true and exitCode: 1.
[unit] In captureWorkingTreeChanges's existing three-hung-call setup with the group-kill seam stubbed, proc.kill still runs exactly three times, preserving the existing killCount assertion.
[unit] In the same three-hung-call setup, captureWorkingTreeChanges still resolves [], preserving its existing best-effort empty-on-failure result.

routing.reasoning: Binding caller-regression story updates existing shared-seam harnesses across three suites without altering credential or authentication behavior.

modifiedFiles.reason: `AC-3 forwards the deadline and kills a hung git` fakes `_gitDeps.spawn` (pid 4242) and reaches the timeout kill; it must also replace `_gitDeps.killProcessGroup` with a recording stub (restored after the test). Its `killed` and `timedOut` assertions stay.

`does not stall when git subprocess hangs (SIGKILL after timeout)` fakes `_gitDeps.spawn` (pid 4242) and reaches three timeout kills; it must also replace `_gitDeps.killProcessGroup` with a recording stub (restored after the test). Its `killCount` of 3 still holds, because `proc.kill` still runs once per call.

the `getUncommittedFilesImpl — BUG-1 pipe-drain regression` suite fakes `_gitDeps.spawn` (pid 4242) with `_gitDeps.gitTimeoutMs` at 50 and reaches the timeout kill; each of its tests must also replace `_gitDeps.killProcessGroup` with a recording stub (restored in `afterEach`). Its existing assertions stay.

userStories.title: A provider tool's cancel grace
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Allow an opt-in provider coding tool to return its own outcome during a bounded post-abort grace.

**Motivation** — after Esc during the `nax-flow__send` push, the transcript says `abandoned: the turn ended`.

**Approach** — **#2901 part 1, cancel grace.** This is opt-in per tool. `ProviderTool` gains `cancelGraceMs?: number`, and `adaptProviderTool` copies it onto the adapted `CodingTool` (`CodingTool.cancelGraceMs?: number`). `nativeBackend` builds a map from qualified tool name to grace for every provider tool that declares one, and passes it to `createSessionInteractionHandler` as `SessionInteractionDeps.cancelGraceByTool`. `runCodingTool` then composes the turn signal and the grace in this order:

1. The signal is already aborted when the call arrives: answer the generic abandoned outcome at once and never call the tool (unchanged).
2. The tool declares no grace (absent from the map): answer the generic abandoned outcome the moment the signal aborts (unchanged).
3. The tool declares a grace: when the signal aborts, wait up to the grace for the tool's own outcome. If it settles in time, that outcome is the answer, with the same handling as an unaborted call: `denied` maps to a denial, `error` throws, `ok` answers. Otherwise answer the generic abandoned outcome, and ignore the late settlement.

A declared grace is normalised before use: a non-finite value or one `<= 0` counts as no grace, and a value above `MAX_CANCEL_GRACE_MS = 10_000` counts as `10_000`. The grace timer is cleared on every settle path. Embedder tools (`invoke`) are unchanged.

**Scope** — In: provider metadata, adaptation, native session-open wiring and coding-tool interaction cancellation, including timers and rejection cleanup. Extend existing provider-adapt, session-interaction and native-backend-providers regressions with fake-clock cases. Out: US-005 owns the concrete flow-send grace declaration, koda HTTP signal propagation and cancelled-create message; embedder grace and late transcript append are excluded.

**Interface** — `ProviderTool` adds `readonly cancelGraceMs?: number`. `CodingTool` adds `readonly cancelGraceMs?: number`. `adaptProviderTool` carries the field only when declared; there is no key otherwise. `nativeBackend` passes `cancelGraceByTool` built from `providerTools.tools`.

```typescript
readonly cancelGraceByTool?: ReadonlyMap<string, number>
readonly timers?: { readonly setTimeout: (fn: () => void, ms: number) => unknown; readonly clearTimeout: (id: unknown) => void }
```

The timers default to the process globals. The module exports `MAX_CANCEL_GRACE_MS = 10_000`. The abandoned outcome is `{ kind: "error", content: 'Tool "<name>" was abandoned: the turn ended.' }`. Rejection within grace is handled exactly as the existing unaborted rejection; a late outcome or rejection is observed but ignored. Preserve existing policy denials, sandbox outcome metadata and current-call cleanup. Use a fake clock passed through SessionInteractionDeps.timers for the direct-handler timing criteria; show regressions fail before implementation without editing source in the test-writing session.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] adaptProviderTool("acme", { localName: "put", ..., cancelGraceMs: 2_000 }) returns a tool whose cancelGraceMs is 2_000.
[unit] adaptProviderTool on a provider tool without cancelGraceMs returns a tool that has no cancelGraceMs key.
[unit] MAX_CANCEL_GRACE_MS exported from session-interaction.ts equals 10_000.

[unit] A handler from createSessionInteractionHandler with cancelGraceByTool mapping acme__put to 500, whose runtime's callTool resolves { kind: "ok", content: "done" } 50 ms after the request signal aborts, answers { answer: "done" } for an acme__put coding-tool request aborted mid-call.

[unit] In the 500 ms grace setup, with callTool resolving { kind: "error", content: "[chat] nothing was pushed" } 50 ms after the abort, onInteraction rejects with an error whose message is [chat] nothing was pushed.

[unit] In the 500 ms grace setup, with callTool resolving { kind: "denied", reason: "no", breach: false } 50 ms after the abort, onInteraction answers { answer: "Denied: no", denied: { reason: "no", breach: false } }.

[unit] In the 500 ms grace setup, with callTool resolving 1 s after the abort (past the 500 ms grace), onInteraction rejects with the message Tool "acme__put" was abandoned: the turn ended. once the fake clock passes 500 ms after the abort, and not before.

[unit] When the signal aborts mid-call for a coding-tool request whose tool is absent from cancelGraceByTool and whose callTool never settles, onInteraction rejects with Tool "<name>" was abandoned: the turn ended. without the fake clock advancing.
[unit] A request whose signal is already aborted when it arrives rejects with the abandoned message and never calls callTool, even when the tool's grace is 500.
[unit] When the signal aborts mid-call for a tool with a grace of NaN, 0 or -5 whose callTool never settles, onInteraction rejects with the abandoned message without the fake clock advancing.
[unit] A grace of 60_000 for a tool whose callTool never settles rejects with the abandoned message once the fake clock passes 10 s after the abort, and not before.
[unit] After a grace-path answer { answer: "done" }, the fake clock reports zero outstanding timers.

[unit] Criteria 4 to 12 above run on a fake clock passed as `SessionInteractionDeps.timers`, never on wall time: the 500 ms grace-expiry test (criterion 7), run on that clock, completes in under 100 ms of wall time.

[unit] Opening a session through nativeBackend with a static provider id acme whose tool put declares cancelGraceMs: 500 and whose run resolves { content: "late" } 50 ms after its signal aborts, then calling opened.turnOpts().interactionHandler.onInteraction for acme__put with a signal aborted mid-call, answers { answer: "late" }.

[unit] A tool with a 500 ms grace whose callTool rejects 1 s after the abort (past the grace) produces no unhandled rejection: the test's unhandled-rejection listener records nothing after the fake clock passes 1 s.
[unit] The same nativeBackend session open with a provider tool that declares no cancelGraceMs and never settles rejects with the abandoned message as soon as the signal aborts.
When a tool declares Infinity as its grace and callTool never settles, aborting onInteraction rejects with the abandoned message without advancing the fake clock.
When callTool rejects inside its declared grace after the signal aborts, onInteraction propagates that rejection as an unaborted call does today.

routing.reasoning: Cross-module session contract and cancellation state machine with tool denial semantics, timer cleanup and late rejection races; session/security override requires strict isolation.

userStories.title: A forget answered pending keeps its note
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Preserve a direct-mode note when a generic memory provider holds its forget pending, on immediate handover and queued delivery.

**Motivation** — A forget the owner rejected silently loses the note from one checkout.

**Approach** — **#2905, a koda-held forget.** Today, under `memory.writeMode: "direct"` (the CLI's mode comes from config; koda answers `202` whatever the local mode is), `forgetLocked` (`packages/nax-agent/src/memory/operations.ts`) deletes the note before the push. `handOverForget` and the drain's `applyPushed` (`delivery.ts`) then accept a `pending` answer without putting it back. The fix has two halves:

- nax-agent (generic): a forget the provider answers `pending` leaves the note in the mirror. On the hand-over path, `handOverForget` writes `previous` back with `restoreForgotten` when `writeMode` is `direct`. On the drain path, the note was deleted when the entry was queued and the entry holds no copy, so `applyPushed` rewinds that scope's pull cursor with the existing `rewindPullCursor(store, scope)` when the entry's `writeMode` is `direct`. A `proposal` entry never deleted its note, so it does not rewind. `rewindPullCursor` lives in `sync-drain.ts`, which already imports `applyPushed` from `delivery.ts`, so calling it from `delivery.ts` would be an import cycle, which `check-import-cycles` fails. It moves to a new leaf module, `packages/nax-agent/src/memory/pull-cursor.ts`, whose only imports are types. `sync-drain.ts` re-exports it, so `internal.ts` and nax's `host-writes.ts` import it unchanged. The same sync's pull then re-reads the scope in full and brings the provider's active row back. A forget answered `deleted` is unchanged.

**Scope** — In: generic memory operations, delivery, cursor-leaf extraction, handover/support extraction and immediate/queued regression tests. Out: US-006 owns koda approval records, refusal resolution and host/list pending markers; this story does not add remote approval markers to the on-disk index or write remote forgets into pending-forgets.jsonl.

**Interface** — `handOverForget` and `applyPushed` implement the pending behavior above. `forgetMemoryNote`'s exported signature and behaviour for every answer other than `pending` under `direct` stay. `drainOutbox` and every other export keep their behaviour.

```typescript
restoreForgotten(input, previous)
rewindPullCursor(store, scope)
```

`operations.ts` is 599 lines against the 600-line source cap enforced by `bun run check:file-sizes`, so the forget hand-over needs room. For example, `forgetLocked`, `handOverForget` and `queuedForget` can move into a new `packages/nax-agent/src/memory/forget-handover.ts`. They share `refreshIndex` (`operations.ts`, not exported) and `FORGET_STATUS_BY_MODE` with code that stays. A new module that imports those back from `operations.ts`, while `operations.ts` imports it, is an import cycle, which `check-import-cycles` fails. Helpers both need can live in a third leaf module that imports neither (for example `packages/nax-agent/src/memory/operations-support.ts`).

Restore the original note before refreshing the handover index, and remove the accepted request from the outbox normally. Preserve write-ahead enqueue order, mirror locks, refusal bookkeeping and proposal-mode behavior. New nax-agent relative source imports must name .ts files. Extend operations-forget and sync-drain/sync regressions with the existing real mirror, provider and clock helpers; demonstrate failure against old code.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] forgetMemoryNote with writeMode: "direct", a mirror holding note x, and a provider whose push resolves { id, status: "pending" } returns status: "pending" and leaves store.readNote("project", "x") equal to the note as it was before the forget.
[unit] In the direct pending-forget setup, the outbox holds no entry for x after the call.
[unit] In the direct pending-forget setup, the memory index the call refreshes still lists x: the note is restored before the index is refreshed.
[unit] forgetMemoryNote with writeMode: "direct" and a provider answering { status: "deleted" } leaves store.readNote("project", "x") returning null.
[unit] forgetMemoryNote with writeMode: "proposal" and a provider answering { status: "pending" } leaves note x in the mirror unchanged.
[unit] applyPushed for a direct-mode forget entry of scope project answered { status: "pending" } sets the store's sync-state cursor.project to null and leaves cursor.user unchanged.
[unit] applyPushed for a forget entry answered { status: "deleted" } deletes the note and leaves the sync-state cursor unchanged.
[unit] applyPushed for a forget entry whose writeMode is proposal, answered { status: "pending" }, leaves the sync-state cursor unchanged and the note in the mirror.

[integration] A sync whose drain pushes a queued direct forget of note x (deleted when queued) to a provider that answers pending, and whose provider pull serves x as active, ends with x in the mirror.

[unit] When the provider is reachable but push rejects a transient network Error during a direct-mode forget, forgetMemoryNote leaves the forget request queued in the outbox for retry, preserving the existing transient-failure behavior.

routing.reasoning: Two durable write paths require different recovery mechanisms, plus cycle-free extractions under hard file-size limits and a real-sync regression.

modifiedFiles.reason: `rewindPullCursor` is removed from this file's own body and re-exported from the new pull-cursor leaf module this story creates; `drainOutbox` and every other export keep their behaviour.

at 599 lines against the 600-line cap, it may hand `handOverForget` and `queuedForget` to the new forget hand-over module this story creates; `forgetMemoryNote`'s exported signature and behaviour for every answer other than `pending` under `direct` stay.

userStories.title: Flow send stops the koda create and says what happened
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Cancel the koda create with the turn signal and preserve flow send's precise cancellation outcome through its opt-in grace.

**Motivation** — An Esc after the push and during `POST /fleet/flows` lets koda create the flow in the background while the chat says "abandoned".

**Approach** — **#2901 part 2, the koda create.** `KodaClient.post` gains an optional third argument `{ signal?: AbortSignal }`, and `KodaClient.get` is unchanged. In `request`, a given signal that aborts before the answer ends the call with a `NaxError` coded `MEMORY_KODA_ABORTED`, and aborts the fetch through the existing `cancel` controller. A signal already aborted when `post` is called rejects with the same error and never calls `fetch`. An answer that arrived before the abort is returned as usual. `createKodaFlow(connection, body, signal?)` passes the signal to `client.post`. In `flow-provider.ts`, `afterAllow` passes its signal to `createFlow`, which passes it to `createKodaFlow`. When the create rejects with `MEMORY_KODA_ABORTED`, the result is the failure `[chat] the turn was cancelled during the koda request; branch <branch> stays pushed and koda may have created the flow; check koda's flows before sending again (a duplicate send is refused with 409)`. The send tool declares `cancelGraceMs: FLOW_SEND_CANCEL_GRACE_MS` (`5_000`), so this answer, and the existing `[chat] the turn was cancelled; nothing was pushed`, reach the transcript.

**Scope** — In: optional POST cancellation, complete-answer race/cleanup, flow-koda and provider signal plumbing, the exact post-push cancellation message, 5000 ms send declaration and regression tests including new flow-provider-cancel.test.ts. Out: US-003 supplies session grace mechanics; US-006 owns memory forget approvals. Do not query koda to resolve a cancelled create, retry it, add grace to other tools, or append results after grace.

**Interface** —

```typescript
post(path: string, body: unknown, opts?: { readonly signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<KodaResponse>
createKodaFlow(connection: KodaFlowConnection, body: FlowCreateBody, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<FlowCreateOutcome>
```

The module exports `FLOW_SEND_CANCEL_GRACE_MS = 5_000`. `createFlow`, `afterAllow` and `sendTool` follow the approach above. Keep `KodaClient.get` unchanged. Abort the fetch using the existing cancel controller and race caller cancellation even if the fetch ignores its signal, covering response-body receipt as the existing timeout does. Keep MEMORY_KODA_TIMEOUT for a request without an external signal that exceeds timeoutMs, classified NaxErrors and secret/header redaction. Once created or held is received, a later abort does not replace that outcome. A failed cancelled push still reports nothing was pushed and never calls createKodaFlow. Preserve the approved-card branch identity and security checks. Extend koda-http.test.ts and flow-koda.test.ts using their dependency seams and demonstrate old-code failures.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] With _kodaClientDeps.fetch faked to answer 201 after 100 ms, createKodaClient(...).post("fleet/flows", body, { signal }) with signal aborted at 10 ms rejects with a NaxError coded MEMORY_KODA_ABORTED.
[unit] In the delayed-201 abort setup, the RequestInit passed to the faked fetch carries a signal that is aborted once the call has rejected.
[unit] post(path, body, { signal }) with signal already aborted rejects MEMORY_KODA_ABORTED and calls the faked fetch zero times.
[unit] post(path, body, { signal }) whose faked fetch answers 201 before signal aborts resolves { status: 201, data }.
[unit] post(path, body) without a third argument, whose fetch answers after the client's timeoutMs, still rejects MEMORY_KODA_TIMEOUT.
[unit] createKodaFlow(connection, body, signal) calls the stubbed client's post with ("fleet/flows", body, { signal }).
[unit] The nax-flow__send tool from createFlowProvider(...).tools() has cancelGraceMs equal to FLOW_SEND_CANCEL_GRACE_MS, which equals 5_000.

[unit] Running the send tool through the _flowProviderDeps harness with an approved card, a commitAndPush that resolves, and a createKodaFlow stub, passes the run context's signal as createKodaFlow's third argument.

[unit] In the approved-card successful-push setup, with createKodaFlow rejecting a NaxError coded MEMORY_KODA_ABORTED, the tool result is the error [chat] the turn was cancelled during the koda request; branch <branch> stays pushed and koda may have created the flow; check koda's flows before sending again (a duplicate send is refused with 409), with <branch> the carded branch.
[unit] In the approved-card successful-push setup, with the signal aborted after createKodaFlow resolves { kind: "created", ... }, the tool result is the same created-flow content as with no abort.

[unit] In the approved-card setup, with commitAndPush rejecting while the signal is aborted, the tool result is still [chat] the turn was cancelled; nothing was pushed and createKodaFlow is never called.
When koda's held-flow answer arrives before the abort lands, flow send returns its normal held-create content rather than a cancelled-create error.

routing.reasoning: Concurrent HTTP answer/abort/deadline handling across an approved outward-facing tool and a credential-bearing client; preserve approval and credential protections with strict TDD isolation.

userStories.title: Koda records and resolves a held forget
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist koda-held forget approvals, reconcile refusals without deleting active notes, and expose pending markers through the host and list.

**Motivation** — two checkouts linked to the same koda project disagree until the first one is reset.

**Approach** — - nax (koda): `KodaApproval` gains `kind?: "save" | "forget"`. An absent `kind`, and any `kind` value other than `"forget"`, reads as a save, so an existing file stays valid and an unknown value never makes the file unusable. An older nax that rewrites the file drops `kind`, which turns a forget record into a save record; that is accepted. `approvalOf` keeps it, and `record` replaces only the record with the same kind, scope and slug. `retire()` in `koda-provider.ts` records a `202` answer with `kind: "forget"` (approval id = `data.id` of the answer, client id = the request's `clientId`) before returning `pending`. A `202` without a string `data.id` is the provider's existing bad-response error. A `record` that rejects (for example `MEMORY_KODA_APPROVALS_READ_FAILED`) is logged as a warn and the forget still resolves `pending`. Koda has already opened the approval, so rejecting the push would queue a retry, and a retry's retire can answer `409`, which the provider reads as `deleted`. Without a record the note stays in the mirror unmarked, and the feed's tombstone still removes it if koda executes the forget. In `koda-pull.ts`, `resolveRecord` treats a forget record by koda's answer: open keeps it; executed drops it (the feed's retired-row tombstone removes the note); gone (`404`) drops it. Refused drops it when this page already carries the slug (the existing `where.pageSlugs` check, which a rewound full re-read hits) or when the mirror holds the slug. Otherwise refused restores koda's active row through the existing `rowRestoration`, or drops the record when koda has no active row. A refused forget never produces a tombstone. The memory host's `readForgetPendingKeys` adds `pendingForgetKey({ scope, slug })` for every koda forget record, so `forgetPendingKeys()` and `renderIndex()` both carry it: `nax memory list` marks the note `(forget pending)`, and so does the index `host.renderIndex()` renders for a session.

**Scope** — In: approvals kind compatibility and replacement identity, recording remote retire approvals, forget-specific pull resolution, host composition and pending-key propagation, existing list behavior, and unit/integration regressions. US-004's put-back of a `pending` forget is what leaves the note in the mirror for this story's `(forget pending)` marker and refused-forget resolution. Out: US-004 owns generic operations/delivery restoration; US-005 owns HTTP and flow-create cancellation. Refused-proposal memory status, remote markers in the on-disk agent index, writing remote approvals into pending-forgets.jsonl and save-versus-pending-forget conflict handling remain excluded.

**Interface** — `KodaApproval` adds `readonly kind?: "save" | "forget"`. `approvalOf`, `createKodaApprovals`, `retire`, `resolveRecord` and `refusedRecord` implement the approach above. `composeKoda` hands back the approvals store it creates alongside the provider, `MemoryParts` gains an optional `kodaApprovals?: KodaApprovals`, and `readForgetPendingKeys` adds the forget records' keys. That is more than the 9 lines `host.ts` has left, so `readForgetPendingKeys` and `pendingForgetKey` can move to a new `packages/nax/src/memory/host-forget-keys.ts`, with `pendingForgetKey` still exported from the `@/memory` barrel.

`host.ts` is at 591 lines against the 600-line cap. `createMemoryHost`'s returned host keeps every member and its behaviour, except that `forgetPendingKeys()` now also holds koda forget records' keys. The barrel keeps exporting `pendingForgetKey`, now from wherever it lives. Records without kind must still be written without it, and unknown kind must normalize to save rather than invalidate the file. Keep file version 1 and atomic/serialized writes. Preserve existing save restoration and resolution budgets. For a refused forget, mirror possession is not a pending-save/clientId check. A restoration emitted on a page keeps its record until the mirror receives it; a non-holdable active row warns `koda approval was not resolved` and retains the record, never synthesizing a rejected tombstone.

Create host-forget-keys.ts and test/unit/memory/koda-pull-forget-approvals.test.ts. Extend koda-approvals.test.ts's exact persisted shapes only where kind was declared; absent kind stays absent. The existing koda-provider-forget-search.test.ts row `["a 202", 202, "pending"]` still resolves pending and now receives one record call with kind forget; its double already supplies record, so alter it only if it asserted no call. Exercise host.renderIndex, forgetPendingKeys and CLI memory list, including a faked-transport forget -> list -> refused sync -> list integration flow. Use existing host-koda and koda-pull-approvals scaffolds rather than duplicating infrastructure. For the isolated approval-resolution criteria, pull the scope's last page and use an otherwise empty feed unless the criterion explicitly supplies a page note; refusal resolution must not remove notes already carried by the export feed. Save and forget records are distinguished for reconciliation only: nax does not acquire or exercise koda's approval authority.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] createKodaApprovals(...).record({ approvalId: "apr_1", kind: "forget", scope: "project", slug: "x", clientId: "c_1" }) followed by list() returns that entry with kind: "forget".
[unit] list() on a file whose entry has no kind field returns that entry with no kind (a save).
[unit] Recording a kind: "forget" entry for project/x after a save entry for project/x leaves both entries in list().
[unit] Recording a second kind: "forget" entry for project/x replaces the first forget entry for project/x.

[unit] The koda provider's push of a forget whose POST memory/notes/<id>/retire answers 202 with data.id "apr_9" calls approvals.record once with { approvalId: "apr_9", kind: "forget", scope, slug, clientId } from the request, and resolves status: "pending".
[unit] A forget whose retire answers 202 without a string data.id rejects with the provider's bad-response error and records nothing.
[unit] A forget whose retire answers 200 records nothing and resolves status: "deleted".
[unit] A pull at the scope's last page, with a forget record for x that GET approvals/<id> answers with an open status, keeps the record and restores no note.
[unit] A pull with a forget record for x answered executed drops the record.
[unit] A pull with an otherwise empty feed page and a forget record for x answered with a refused status, while the mirror holds x, drops the record and the page carries no note for x.

[unit] A pull with a forget record for x answered with a refused status, while the mirror does not hold x and koda's active-row lookup returns a holdable row for x, carries that row's note for x in the page and keeps the record.
[unit] A pull with a forget record for x answered with a refused status, while the mirror does not hold x and koda's lookup returns no active row, drops the record and the page carries no note for x.
[unit] No refused forget record produces a note whose status is rejected.
[unit] A pull with a forget record whose approval read answers 404 drops the record.
[unit] A pull whose page already carries a note for x, with a forget record for x answered with a refused status, drops the record and adds no second note for x to the page.

[unit] A pull with a forget record for x answered with a refused status, while the mirror does not hold x and koda's active row for x is not a note the mirror can hold, keeps the record, logs the warn koda approval was not resolved, and the page carries no note for x.
[unit] A forget whose retire answers 202 with data.id "apr_9" while approvals.record rejects MEMORY_KODA_APPROVALS_READ_FAILED resolves status: "pending" and logs one warn naming the slug and apr_9.
[unit] list() on a file whose entry has kind: "later" returns that entry read as a save, and the other entries of the file unchanged.

[unit] renderIndex() of a koda-backed memory host whose approvals store holds a forget record for project/x, with note x in the mirror, renders the x entry marked as forget pending, as it does for a local recorded forget.
[unit] forgetPendingKeys() of a koda-backed memory host whose approvals store holds a forget record for project/x and a save record for project/y returns a set containing project/x and not project/y.
[unit] nax memory list through a host whose forgetPendingKeys() returns project/x, with note x in the mirror, prints the x line ending in ' (forget pending)'.

[integration] With a faked koda transport, a nax memory forget x whose retire answers 202, followed by nax memory list, prints x with ' (forget pending)'. A sync whose approval read then answers a refused status, followed by nax memory list, prints x without the suffix.

routing.reasoning: Durable memory reconciliation spans approvals persistence, provider, pull and host composition with backward-compatible kind parsing; complex three-session-lite fits this data-integrity change without treating status tracking as an authentication or authorization implementation.

modifiedFiles.reason: the table row `["a 202", 202, "pending"]` builds the provider with an approvals double that may not expect a `record` call; the row keeps answering `pending`; its approvals double already supplies `record`, and now receives one `record` call with `kind: "forget"`, so no change to the double is needed unless the test asserts the double was never called.

the assertions on the written file shape (`{ version: 1, approvals: [...] }` entries with exactly `approvalId`, `scope`, `slug`, `clientId`) gain `kind` where a record was made with one; a record made without `kind` is still written without it.

at 591 lines against the 600-line cap, it may hand `readForgetPendingKeys` and `pendingForgetKey` to the new host forget-keys module this story creates, and re-export `pendingForgetKey`; `createMemoryHost`'s returned host keeps every member and its behaviour, except that `forgetPendingKeys()` now also holds koda forget records' keys.
the barrel keeps exporting `pendingForgetKey`, now from wherever it lives.

userStories.title: No files-placeholder warning for an orchestrator test command
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Suppress the misleading missing-{{files}} warning for declared turbo/nx test commands while preserving equality warnings.

**Motivation** — every turbo/nx monorepo config gets a warning whose advice ("add `{{files}}`") cannot be followed: orchestrators take no test paths, and `resolveQualityTestCommands` never substitutes `{{files}}` into the root template in that mode.

**Approach** — **#2908.** `isMonorepoOrchestratorCommand` moves from `packages/nax/src/test-runners/scoped-selection.ts` into a new leaf module, `packages/nax/src/test-runners/orchestrator-command.ts`, whose only import is `normalizeCommandSpec` and the `QualityCommandSpec` type from `@nathapp/nax-agent/internal`. `scoped-selection.ts` re-exports it, so every existing importer is unchanged. `warnScopedTestCommand` imports the leaf directly, by the relative path `../test-runners/orchestrator-command` (a value import of `@/test-runners/<file>` from `src/` is forbidden by `check-alias-internals` because `src/test-runners/index.ts` exists); importing `scoped-selection.ts` from config would pull `@/logger` and `verification/smart-runner` into config's import graph. After the equality check and before the `{{files}}` check, `warnScopedTestCommand` returns without a warning when `isMonorepoOrchestratorCommand(test)` is true for the declared `quality.commands.test`.

**Scope** — In: moving the unchanged predicate to its leaf, retaining scoped-selection's use/re-export and inserting the warning early return in config-guards.ts without exceeding its 600-line cap (currently 593). Extend config-guards and predicate/re-export tests. Out: unrelated cancellation, memory and workflow stories; no reading review.commands.test, substituting files through root orchestrators, or changing RunCommand testScoped's package-filtered command.

**Interface** —

```typescript
isMonorepoOrchestratorCommand(command: QualityCommandSpec): boolean
warnScopedTestCommand(conf: Record<string, unknown>, warn?: (msg: string) => void): void
```

`isMonorepoOrchestratorCommand` is removed from scoped-selection.ts's own body and re-exported from the new leaf; every importer keeps importing it from here unchanged. Keep its every-command turbo/nx detection and identity, and keep equality as the highest-priority warning. Only quality.commands.test establishes the exemption: a turbo testScoped alone still warns when test is missing. The warning remains advisory, not a config rejection.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] isMonorepoOrchestratorCommand("npx turbo test") imported from packages/nax/src/test-runners/orchestrator-command.ts returns true.
[unit] isMonorepoOrchestratorCommand imported from scoped-selection.ts is the same function as the one from orchestrator-command.ts.
[unit] warnScopedTestCommand({ quality: { commands: { test: "npx turbo test", testScoped: "npx turbo test --filter=[HEAD^1]" } } }, warn) never calls warn.
[unit] warnScopedTestCommand with test: "nx affected -t test" and testScoped: "nx affected -t test --base=HEAD~1" never calls warn.

[unit] warnScopedTestCommand with test: "npx turbo test" and testScoped: "npx turbo test" calls warn once with quality.commands.testScoped equals quality.commands.test, so every scoped run is the full suite.
[unit] warnScopedTestCommand with test: "bun test" and testScoped: "bun test --bail" still calls warn once with the {{files}} placeholder message.
[unit] warnScopedTestCommand with testScoped: "npx turbo test --filter=[HEAD^1]" and no test command still calls warn once with the {{files}} placeholder message.

routing.reasoning: Small behavior change and compatibility-preserving leaf extraction across existing modules; clear precedence and import-graph constraints.

modifiedFiles.reason: `isMonorepoOrchestratorCommand` is removed from this file's own body and re-exported from the new leaf module this story creates; every importer keeps importing it from here unchanged.

userStories.title: The branch-review line counts triaged deferred minors
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make branch review's step line explain the deferred-minor fix-now/leave decisions that cause branch-fix to run.

**Motivation** — someone watching a run reads "no findings" and then sees a branch-fix session start with no reason given.

**Approach** — **#2909.** `branchReviewStep` appends the deferred-minor triage to its `log.done` text whenever the record holds deferred minors, counted after this review's triage is applied: `; deferred minors: <n> fix-now, <m> leave`. Nothing else changes, including the `branch fix: N item(s)` ledger note, which stays `NO_MIRROR`.

**Scope** — In: branchReviewStep in feature-steps.ts and its feature-machine-log regression harness. Count rec.minors after applying this verdict's minorTriage with unmentioned minors defaulting to leave; do not count newly reported review minors as deferred ones. Out: other stories' git, session, flow, memory and config changes; do not mirror the branch-fix ledger note or change review routing, finding assignment or fix policy.

**Interface** —

```typescript
MinorTriageDecision = "fix-now" | "leave"
```

Keep describeFindings unchanged. Append the exact suffix to log.done's existing text only for records with deferred minors and before the run-log formatter's elapsed-time suffix. Preserve no-deferred-minors and skipped-review behavior, review artifacts and the record patch. Reuse the existing structured workflow log sink and feature-machine environment; write regressions for clean findings, important findings, no deferred minors and omitted triage decisions before implementing.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] A feature-machine run whose branch review returns no findings and triages two of three deferred minors fix-now logs a branch-review: step line containing no findings; deferred minors: 2 fix-now, 1 leave.
[unit] A branch review with one important finding and one deferred minor triaged leave logs a step line ending, before the elapsed time, with ; deferred minors: 0 fix-now, 1 leave.
[unit] A branch review of a record with no deferred minors logs a step line with no deferred minors text.
[unit] Given one deferred minor that the review's minorTriage does not mention, branchReviewStep logs the suffix ; deferred minors: 0 fix-now, 1 leave, counting the omitted minor as leave.

[unit] When branchReviewStep receives a record with deferred minors but no seed, it still logs branch-review: skipped (no seed) followed only by the existing elapsed-time suffix, without appending deferred-minor triage.

routing.reasoning: Single production logging change using existing triage state and feature-machine log tests; no new dependencies or workflow transitions.

No implementation or validation commands were run while drafting this PRD.

Architecture and conventions: docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:141 defines the package direction and publication boundaries, and :155 lists the 600-line hard source cap, dependency seams, typed errors and concurrency conventions. nax-agent is Node-compatible source developed/tested with Bun, whereas nax is Bun-native. Keep spawning behind runtimeSpawn, use #src/ aliases in nax-agent and .ts extensions for its relative source imports, and cross the package boundary through named public exports or @nathapp/nax-agent/internal. Never import nax into nax-agent. Preserve public and internal entry identity when moving helpers. ProviderTool and CodingTool are already publicly re-exported (packages/nax-agent/src/index.ts:474 and :533); the grace properties are additive, not new unrelated public exports. Review the declaration snapshot if emitted API changes require it, but do not expose private seams from the root entry or bump package versions. Read the package rules and architecture index before implementing; run targeted bun tests with an explicit path, not bare bun test. Regression tests must demonstrably fail against old behavior. Use existing helpers instead of reimplementing fake clocks, loggers, spawns or temporary-directory fixtures. Quality gates belong to implementation validation, not acceptance criteria.

Add killProcessGroup to this exact dependency object, spawn detached, and route both kill paths through group-then-direct SIGKILL in separate try blocks without changing arguments or result shapes. The existing helper at packages/nax-agent/src/internal/process-kill.ts:30 rejects unsafe pids, signals -pid, suppresses ESRCH single-pid fallback when requested, and reports non-ESRCH failures as sent. Therefore the explicit proc.kill must still run, including on Windows or after group-kill errors. packages/nax-agent/src/internal/argv-exec.ts:75 already exposes the equivalent group-kill seam and uses the runtime abstraction. packages/nax/src/utils/git.ts:5 imports and :8 re-exports the identical _gitDeps object, so nax tests can intercept it without new production wrappers. captureWorkingTreeChanges is at :349 and its calls forward timeoutRetryGitTimeoutMs at :358. packages/nax/src/bot/git.ts:58 forwards the timeout to gitWithTimeout at :74 while retaining hook suppression, authenticated argv and environment handling. Preserve those behaviors; no credentials need changing. NO_TERMINAL_PROMPT is at packages/nax/src/utils/git.ts:15. Detached git loses its controlling terminal; askpass and credential helpers remain usable, but ssh's own /dev/tty passphrase or host-key prompts now fail immediately. Patch and restore _gitDeps.killProcessGroup locally in all five existing kill-reaching suites as part of their owning stories; do not change the shared fake pid or global preload. Agent suites are packages/nax-agent/test/unit/internal/git-env.test.ts:176 (abort tests, including already-aborted and stalled-pipe paths) and packages/nax-agent/test/unit/tools/git-commit.test.ts:294 (hung check-ignore, shrinks timeout at :303). nax suites are packages/nax/test/unit/utils/git.test.ts:185 (three hangs, killCount remains 3 at :218), packages/nax/test/unit/bot/git.test.ts:35, and packages/nax/test/unit/review/runner.test.ts:403 (timeout override at :425 and restoration at :430). The new POSIX integration test is the intentional exception using a real spawn and group kill: wrap the runtime spawn to capture git pid, abort after 200 ms, inspect ps pid/pgid, allow at most 2 seconds for the group to disappear, skip where process groups are unsupported and ensure child/seam cleanup even after failure. Existing sync-drain/sync tests and integration memory suites cover scheduling and cursor preservation. This generic fix must land before koda marking/resolution.

US-005 HTTP and flow cancellation: packages/nax/src/memory/koda-http.ts:51 defines KodaClient with a two-argument post, :269 request races perform against a cancellable deadline, :258 perform includes response-body reading, :287 preserves classified NaxErrors and :291 aborts its controller in finally. outOfScope: `nax memory status` reporting a refused koda proposal, whether a save or a forget: status reads only the outbox today, and a refused koda record is resolved without a report. This is a follow-up to #2905.

The `(forget pending)` marker in the on-disk `index.md` that nax-agent's `refreshIndex` writes, and `index-render.ts`'s own reads, for a koda-held forget: they read only the outbox and the local `pending-forgets.jsonl` record. `nax memory list` and `host.renderIndex()` (which read `readForgetPendingKeys`) do mark it.
Writing a koda-held forget into the mirror's `pending-forgets.jsonl` record: `nax memory approve <slug>` would then retire the note locally without koda's decision.
A save of a slug while a koda forget of it is pending: the two records coexist and each resolves on its own.
A cancel grace for embedder tools (`EmbedderTool`), or a grace that any tool other than `nax-flow__send` declares.
Appending a tool's late result to the transcript after its grace has passed.
Asking koda after a cancelled create whether the flow exists: the result says the outcome is unknown.
Mirroring the `branch fix: N item(s): ...` ledger note to the run log.
Reading `review.commands.test` in `warnScopedTestCommand`: only the declared `quality.commands.test` decides the orchestrator check.

Killing git when nax itself exits mid-call: a detached git no longer receives the terminal's SIGINT, and the timeout timer dies with nax, so a nax killed during `botGit` or `commitAndPush` can leave git and its helpers running (`argvExec` has the same trait).
Running scoped test files through an orchestrator at the repo root: `RunCommand testScoped` keeps running the package-filtered command.
Changing `makeSpawnResult`'s default pid in `packages/test-kit`, or installing a default `_gitDeps.killProcessGroup` stub in a test preload.
Keeping a terminal for git's ssh transport: a detached git cannot answer an ssh passphrase or host-key prompt on the terminal.
